Only loop discovery sits inside the boundary now, and a test asserts a post-generation failure runs the request exactly once.
title: Synchronous wrapper can retry work on a new event loop after runtime failure

note: The worker caught four exception classes, so OSError, ImportError, TimeoutError, cancellation paths and loop-closure errors exited the thread without enqueueing the None sentinel and left queue.get blocked indefinitely. The sentinel is posted in a finally, and _post tolerates a closed loop by setting the stop flag rather than raising out of the post.
title: Unexpected worker exceptions can leave the stream waiting forever

note: The worker scheduled put_nowait into an unbounded asyncio.Queue and could outrun a slow consumer, retaining every chunk produced. The producer now waits while qsize is at or above _STREAM_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER and stops immediately when the consumer sets the stop flag.
title: Streaming uses an unbounded queue with no producer backpressure

note: The stream yielded raw generate_step text until EOS with no stop sequences or role-continuation truncation, so a model that began writing the next turn streamed its ChatML role markers to the consumer as its own answer. _STREAM_STOP_SEQUENCES and _stream_stop_index cut the stream at the earliest marker, emitting only the text before it.
title: Streaming bypasses stop, sentinel, schema, and response controls

note: The GPU sentinel bounds how long a call waits to START; nothing bounded how long generation could then run on a non-preemptible lane. The await is bounded by _accepted_generation_budget_s (clamped, finite, non-negative), a timeout records a degradation and marks the lane's last_error, and the comment states plainly that mlx generation cannot be interrupted mid-call so the thread may still be unwinding.
title: Generation has no absolute request deadline

note: max_tokens was already clamped by _bounded_max_tokens; prefill was not, going from kwargs straight into the ChatML assistant turn with no type check or length bound so a non-string raised inside formatting and a large one consumed the window. _bounded_prefill coerces and caps at _MAX_PREFILL_CHARS.
title: Text generation forwards unbounded max_tokens and prefill

note: Readiness required only path existence and mlx_lm.load returning two objects, and every caller reads 'loaded' as readiness — including the fallback deciding whether to swap lanes. _readiness_probe runs off the loop: a tokenizer round trip plus vocabulary-size agreement between tokenizer and model, since a tokenizer that can emit ids the model lacks produces garbage rather than an error. A lane that fails stays unavailable with the reason recorded.
title: Loaded objects are declared ready without identity or inference proof

note: The adapter attached whenever adapter_config.json existed. _adapter_compatibility reads the config, requires adapter weights beside it, and requires the declared base model to match the lane's model directory; an adapter naming no base is refused because compatibility that cannot be established is not compatibility. A refusal loads the base Cortex and is recorded.
title: Adapter load is gated only by adapter_config existence

note: Concurrent ensure_listener_started calls could both observe None and both subscribe, and _running started true and was never cleared with no cancel, unsubscribe or join anywhere. Start is serialized under a lock, a done-callback clears the handle so a dead listener can be restarted, and stop_listener cancels, joins under _LISTENER_STOP_TIMEOUT_S and releases the subscription.
title: Update listener is race-created and has no shutdown path

note: Malformed-event handling was already broadened in an earlier pass; what remained was that nothing reset _listener_task, so a listener killed by anything outside the caught classes left the handle set and update handling could never restart. The done-callback clears it and records the exit reason.
title: Malformed events permanently kill update handling

note: CancelledError cleared and released the lane lease immediately, so a new load could take the lease while the previous owned thread still held GPU sentinel ownership. _await_sentinel_idle observes the sentinel free (off the loop, bounded by _CANCELLED_LOAD_DRAIN_S) before release, and records when it could not, so the next holder is never handed a lane still in use silently.
title: Load cancellation releases the lane while the model call may still be unwinding

note: unload_models cleared every reference and reclaimed the MLX cache only if the sentinel could be acquired, returning as though unload had completed when it could not — a caller unloading to free memory was told nothing while weights stayed resident. The failed acquisition records a degradation naming cache_reclaimed=False.
title: Failed final MLX cache acquisition is silently treated as unload completion

note: The estimator was pinned and the ARCHITECTURE it estimated against was not. The preregistration now pins a compute profile, every trial receipt must carry it, and the profile's own shapes must reconcile with the declared parameter count (embeddings + attention projections + SwiGLU) inside a stated tolerance. FLOPs were already recomputed from counters by the pinned ledger; what was missing was any tie between that arithmetic and the 32B-class model the claim is about.

layer_apps was a free-standing integer beside a receipt counting the same quantity, with a ceiling that only excluded a 64-bit overflow. It must now equal the receipt's transformer_layer_apps total, be a whole number of stack passes against the profile's depth, and stay inside a preregistered per-trial forward-pass budget. Per-counter policy maxima beyond layer applications remain out of scope: the remaining counters have no preregistered budget.

The certificate compared treatment against its ablation and stopped. A bundle now carries release readiness: the previous certificate it is measured against with that release's success rate, latency and compute; a safety suite whose digest was preregistered with cases run and violations found; and a calibration receipt with a measured expected calibration error. Each is held to a preregistered budget, and a first release must say so explicitly rather than omitting the section.

params_unchanged rests on a fixed-stride canary over the parameter tree, hashed before and after. The certificate now measures that canary's tensor coverage from both snapshots, takes the weaker side, refuses coverage below a preregistered floor, and carries PARAMETER_INTEGRITY_ATTESTATION so a sampled comparison cannot read as a Merkle root over every tensor byte. Signed pre/post roots remain out of scope: no signing chain exists for worker measurements. An external frontier control is exempt because its weights are not measurable here.

Breadth was two unique non-empty domain strings. The preregistration now pins a taxonomy by digest, every domain must appear in it, and the domains must land in distinct capability classes. The ontology is carried in the bundle and pinned rather than fetched from an external registry.

Episode and request ids only had to be non-empty and globally unique. Each is now derived from the trial's own record — arm, trial id, task id, task payload digest, output digest, worker boot id and evaluation start — so swapping identifiers between trials is caught even though both remain unique.

Arm-visible information receipts had to match each other with nothing tying either to the preregistration, so both arms could share the same undeclared context and policy. Decode, tool and verifier policies inside each information receipt are now pinned to the preregistration. Tool policy per trial was already pinned. Loading and semantically comparing the raw information bundles is out of scope: the certificate holds digests, not the payloads.

The preregistration freeze was a producer-supplied dict and timestamp. Its digest must now be a leaf in an append-only log whose root is pinned in the trust config; certification recomputes the RFC 6962 root from the audit path and requires it to reach the pinned root, and requires the log entry to predate the first task generated.

frozen_at, task_generated_at, evaluation_started_at and committed_at were ordinary numbers inside signed payloads. Both the preregistration and the task commitment are now anchored in the pinned transparency log with ordering enforced against task generation and evaluation start, so backdating requires forging a hash chain against a root the producer does not control. Per-trial evaluation times remain producer-asserted; the anchored events are the two that must precede the run.

The signer payload repeated trust-pin values, so a signature proved key possession and no work. Each attestation now binds the digest of the raw artifact receipt, which comes only from opening the artifact files. VERIFIER_EXECUTION_ATTESTATION names the limit: no measured environment attests that the pinned verifier binary is what ran.

Build, worker binary, provenance and source-commit identifiers were accepted for looking like hashes, with nothing required between them. A release attestation now ties all four to one builder's claim that rebuilding the named commit produces this binary. BUILD_PROVENANCE_ATTESTATION names the limit: nothing re-runs the build and no release signature is checked.

A Claim carried name, statement, tier, evidence and a wall-clock time, so a reproducible experiment and an unreproducible one produced identical tiers. Claims now carry ExperimentProvenance — task manifest, checkpoint, schedule, verifier version and environment — plus the grader's own source digest, which is the one field nobody has to be trusted for. Any missing field caps the tier at CONJECTURE and the gaps are named in the evidence. REFUTED is exempt: downgrading an unreproducible failure would turn missing paperwork into good news. The frontier certificate supplies all five and keeps PROVEN. Dependency lock and full environment capture remain the caller's to hash; the certificate records what it was given.

Factorial arms were graded independently and any PROVEN or SUPPORTED arm joined attribution, with Holm applied only across families inside a claim. Holm now also runs across the arms, using each arm's smallest within-claim adjusted p, and attribution requires the arm-level adjusted p to clear the family-wise alpha. The result publishes the pre-correction list, the per-arm adjusted p and the arm count so the correction is visible rather than implied.
